Question Paper  
Exam Date & Time: 26-Dec-2025 (09:30 AM - 12:30 PM)  
  
  
  MANIPAL ACADEMY OF HIGHER EDUCATION  
  FIRST SEMESTER B.TECH. DEGREE EXAMINATIONS - DEC 2025 / JAN 2026  
  SUBJECT: PHY 1071/PHY_1071 ENGINEERING PHYSICS  
  ENGINEERING PHYSICS [PHY 1071]  
Marks: 50                                                                                                          Duration: 180 mins.  
  
  A  
Answer all the questions.  
  
1A)               Derive the relation between different Einstein Coefficients at thermal equilibrium.                          (5)  
  Discuss the nature of emission for hf < < KT.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO1" / Cognitive Level: "Understand"  
  
1B)               A quantum simple harmonic oscillator consists of an electron bounded by a restoring force                    (3)  
  proportional to its displacement relative to an equilibrium position. The photon of 550 nm is used to  
  excite the oscillator to its first excited state from the ground state. Calculate the proportionality  
  constant and energy of the first excited state.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO3" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
1C)               State whether the given statement is true or false and justify your answer. 'At room temperature the (2)  
  probability of finding an electron at the Fermi level is 0.5',  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO3" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
2A)               With the help of schematic diagram describe how the Davisson-Germer experiment confirmed the                 (5)  
  wave nature of electrons.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO2" / Cognitive Level: "Understand"  
  
2B)               A 30 eV electron and proton are incident on a square barrier of height 40 eV. What is the probability (3)  
  that the electron and proton will tunnel through the barrier if its width is 0.10 nm.  
  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO3" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
2C)               State whether the wavefunction                                            is physically acceptable or not in (2)  
  
  
  the finite potential well with finite height 'U' and length 'L'. Justify your answer.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO3" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
3A)               Derive an expression for density-of-states.                                                                  (5)  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO3" / Cognitive Level: "Understand"  
  
3B)               The frequency of photon that causes v = 0 to v = 1 transition in the CO molecule is 6.42 x 1013 Hz.          (3)  
  Ignore any changes in the rotational energy.  
  Page #1

(a) Calculate the force constant k for this molecule.  
  (b) What is the maximum classical amplitude of vibration for this molecule in the v = 0 vibrational  
  state                                           .  
  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO3" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
3C)            The Fermi level in silver is 5.5 eV at zero kelvin. Calculate the number of free electrons per unit          (2)  
  volume.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO3" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
4A)            What are the factors on which the electric field at some point P near a dipole in a dielectric material (5)  
  depends? Obtain a relationship between the polarizability and the relative permittivity of dielectric  
  materials.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO4" / Cognitive Level: "Understand"  
  
4B)            The atomic weight of Si is 28 and has a density of 2.33 g cm-3 and each atom has polarizability of 2 (3)  
  ×10-40 F m2 . Calculate the ratio of internal field to external field in the case of Si. Given 0ε = 8.854  
  ×10 -12 F/m.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO4" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
4C)            State whether the given statement is true or false and justify your answer. "The density of states in        (2)  
  a bulk material can be obtained using quantum free electron theory because the energy levels of  
  electrons are treated as continuous."  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO3" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
5A)            What are biomaterials? Explain its various biomedical applications with suitable examples.                   (5)  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO5" / Cognitive Level: "Understand"  
  
5B)            Explain how nanotechnology is applied in microelectronics, optoelectronics and medical                       (3)  
  applications.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO5" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
5C)            State whether the given statement is true or false and justify your answer. "The electrical resistivity      (2)  
  of metallic glasses is high and remains almost constant with temperature."  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO5" / Cognitive Level: "Application"
